A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same rePIRL research work, including Sections 1–6 and Appendices A–E. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that the text, equations, tables and figures are available without material gaps.

before.justification: v2 reports original math/coding benchmark experiments and PRM applications in Section 4, with additional evaluation results, ablations and training dynamics in Appendices C–E.

after.justification: v3 retains the original benchmark experiments, application results, ablations and training-dynamics analyses in Section 4 and Appendices C–E.

M1.justification: The alternating PRM/policy algorithm, architectures and intended maximum-entropy objective are unchanged. Equation (6) corrects an inconsistent expansion; its entropy-bonus form and Appendix A.1 already express the retained objective in v2.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven math/coding benchmarks, Eurus training data, test-time training/scaling scenarios and MATH-based hard-problem training. Appendix dataset and expert-trajectory coverage also matches.

E2.justification: Table 2 retains BC, KTO, RL-Tango, MCTS, PRIME, RLOO and SFT+RLOO. Comparator membership also matches in the application experiments, entropy comparison and Appendices C–E.

E3.justification: The model configurations, data splits, two-epoch training budget, checkpoint selection and decoding protocols are unchanged. Appendix C retains non-greedy pass@1 evaluation at temperature 0.6 with 16 responses per prompt.

E4.justification: Both retain the PRM-only experiment and ablations of expert models, reward-model sizes, RL algorithms, importance sampling and corrected trajectories. The entropy and training-dynamics analyses are also unchanged.

E5.justification: Appendix C and Table 4 retain the same average-pass-rate estimator using 16 independent responses per question. Run/seed disclosure, uncertainty reporting and statistical-testing practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All reported results and plotted trends match. For example, Table 2 retains rePIRL math/coding averages of 33.5%/27.7% for Qwen2.5-3B and 41.6%/39.8% for Qwen3-4B; application and appendix results are likewise identical.

T1.justification: Equation (6) changes +β E[log π] to -β E[log π], restoring equality with the entropy bonus +β H(π) and consistency with Appendix A.1. The theorem, propositions and proof steps otherwise remain unchanged; Appendix A.4 only renames a loss symbol.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about minimal-assumption PRM learning, unifying prior methods, benchmark effectiveness and downstream PRM applications.

C2.justification: The interpretations of performance, sparse rewards, entropy preservation, training stability and computational overhead are unchanged. The model-family restrictions and future scaling directions also remain the same.

D1.justification: Hyperparameters, data filtering, hardware, training-time figures and inference instructions match across Section 4.1, Section 5 and Appendix B/Table 3. Code-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The citations, bibliography and positioning relative to supervised PRMs, MCTS, DPO/DQO, PRIME, intrinsic rewards and earlier inverse-RL work are unchanged.

P1.justification: Appendix A.4 replaces L_entropy with L_CE in two displayed equations, clarifying the cross-entropy loss label. The arXiv version/date stamp changes; prose and section organization otherwise match.

P2.justification: All seven tables and four figures retain their structure, captions, axes, legends and placement. Page organization is unchanged, with no added, removed or redesigned displays.

improvement.justification: v3 fixes the entropy sign in Equation (6), removing an inconsistency with the stated objective and Appendix A.1, and clarifies the cross-entropy loss label in Appendix A.4. These localized corrections improve mathematical accuracy and clarity while leaving the method, empirical evidence and substantive claims unchanged.
